tag.name: mail
tag.description: Inbound mail catcher (any address at the mail domain, popped per address), outbound send through SES with generated, saved or received attachments, and an attachment store with text search inside PDF, Office and text files.

get.summary: Take the next captured email for an address
get.description:
Returns the next unread message for `address` and advances the pointer. Any message sent to `<anything>@<mail domain>` is captured and queued per recipient address.

`attachments` is always a list of `{filename, ref, bytes}`; each `ref` is an opaque 10-character token into the temporary received-attachment store (7-day expiry) - use it with mail/attachments/get, mail/attachments/find, mail/attachments/save (to keep it) or mail/send (to forward it).

Nothing unread: 200 with `exhausted: true` and `body: null`. `pending: true` (also exhausted) means a message has been claimed by the receiver but is not written yet - call again, it has NOT been consumed.

`wait` holds the request open until a message arrives. With `wait`, `grace` defaults to 2: when nothing is unread, the most recently delivered message is offered again if it arrived within that many seconds, flagged `repeat: true`. This stops a message being missed in the gap between one polled request ending and the next starting. Do NOT use `wait` in a load test - each waiting call holds a concurrent Lambda execution for its whole duration.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Recipient address the mail was sent to (any local part at the mail domain). Case-insensitive.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Seconds to hold the request open when the inbox is empty, returning the moment a message arrives. 0-20, default 0; larger values are clamped (API Gateway abandons a request at 29 s). Every response carries waitedMs.

parameters.name: grace
parameters.description: Seconds during which the most recently delivered message is re-offered (repeat:true) when nothing is unread. Default 2 when wait is used, 0 otherwise; max 60. Set grace=0 for strict one-message-per-call behaviour - a drain loop that pops until exhausted should do so.

get.summary: Rewind an address's pointer to its first message
get.description: Messages are kept; the next pop returns message 1 again. `reset: false` when the address has never received mail.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Recipient address the mail was sent to (any local part at the mail domain). Case-insensitive.

get.summary: Delete every captured email for an address
get.description: Deletes all messages and the pointer for `address`. `deleted` counts messages. Received attachments are not deleted here; they expire on their own after 7 days.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Recipient address the mail was sent to (any local part at the mail domain). Case-insensitive.

get.description:
Sends a real email through SES. Three forms:

* **GET** - everything in the query string, message in `body`.
* **POST, any non-JSON Content-Type** - the request body is the message.
* **POST, `Content-Type: application/json`** - structured: `{"body": "...", "attachments": [{"filename": "a.pdf", "key": "saved-key"}, {"ref": "rb0q4ipfcu"}]}` for several attachments (each item has exactly one of `key` or `ref`; `filename` optional). Cannot be combined with the attachment query parameters. A JSON-looking body sent WITHOUT the JSON content type goes out as literal text and the response carries `warning`.

Attachment caps: 28000 KB raw in total (SESv2 stops at 40 MB after base64). The recipient is the real limit: Outlook.com/iCloud 20 MB, Yahoo 25 MB, Microsoft 365 36 MB, Gmail 50 MB on the wire. Over 20 MB the response adds `deliverabilityWarning`, `messageMb` and `refusedBy`; it is still a 200 because SES accepted it - the refusal comes back later as a bounce. To test big attachments end to end, send to an address at the mail domain and pop it back.

`sentTime` (epoch seconds) is directly comparable with `receivedTime` from mail/pop. SES refusing the message is a 502.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Sender. Must be an address at the service's mail domain (or a subdomain of it) - the SES-verified identity. A display name is allowed: `Tester <test@example.com>`. Anything else is a 403.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Single recipient. Permitted: any address at the mail domain itself (so you can pop it straight back), or an address/domain on the deployment's allow-list (ALLOWED_TO / ALLOWED_DOMAINS; a `*.example.com` entry admits any subdomain but not example.com itself). Anything else is a 403 listing what is permitted.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: Subject line.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: Message text (plain). Required for GET.

parameters.name: attachmentkb
parameters.description: Attach a generated random-text file of exactly this many KB (1-6000). Mutually exclusive with key and ref.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Attach the SAVED attachment stored under this key (mail/attachments/save or upload/url). 404 if not found. Mutually exclusive with attachmentkb and ref.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: Attach a RECEIVED attachment straight from the temporary store (ref from mail/pop) - no need to save it first. 404 if expired. Mutually exclusive with attachmentkb and key.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Filename shown in the email ('.txt' appended if it has no extension). Defaults to the key, the received attachment's original filename, or a random name for generated text. A generated attachment (no key or ref) named *.pdf is a real PDF made as by mail/attachments/make: attachmentkb and/or pages size it, the *64 values are UTF-8 text placed on the first, middle and last page, and password, seed and paper apply.

parameters.name: prepend64
parameters.description: Base64 bytes to insert at the start of the attachment (e.g. a scanner test signature). Applies to generated, saved or received attachments; on its own it creates an attachment from just these bytes. With a generated *.pdf filename: UTF-8 text placed by page instead (see mail/attachments/make).

parameters.name: overwrite64
parameters.description: Base64 bytes to write over the middle of the attachment (same length replaced). With a generated *.pdf filename: UTF-8 text placed by page instead (see mail/attachments/make).

parameters.name: append64
parameters.description: Base64 bytes to append to the end of the attachment. With a generated *.pdf filename: UTF-8 text placed by page instead (see mail/attachments/make).

parameters.name: pages
parameters.description: Pages of a generated PDF attachment (needs filename=*.pdf), 1-500.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Password-protect a generated PDF attachment (AES-256; attachmentkb up to 2048).

parameters.name: password64
parameters.description: Base64 of the UTF-8 password.

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: Repeatable generated PDF attachment.

parameters.name: paper
parameters.description: a4 (default) or letter, for a generated PDF attachment.

pdf.description: Generated PDF attachments only: pages, paddingBytes, encrypted, placement and seed, as from mail/attachments/make.

403.description: `from` is not at the mail domain, or `to` is not a permitted recipient.

get.summary: Save a received attachment under a key (promote)
get.description:
Stores a file in the SAVED attachment store under `key` (overwrites; kept until deleted), so it can be sent with mail/send, read with mail/attachments/text, searched with mail/attachments/find, or compared with mail/attachments/compare. Pass `filename` (with its extension) to name it. Two sources:

1. **POST** with the file as the request body, up to 4096 KB, in either form:
   * **raw bytes** with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` (what `fetch(url, {method:'POST', body: blob})` or `curl --data-binary @file.pdf -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream'` sends), or
   * **base64 text** of the file (standard or URL-safe, padding optional) with any other content type, e.g. `text/plain`.
   Raw bytes sent with any other content type (e.g. `application/pdf`) are refused with a 400, because the gateway would corrupt them. Use mail/attachments/upload/url for anything larger.
2. **GET or POST with `ref`** - promote a received attachment (S3-to-S3 copy, no body, up to 102400 KB). `filename` renames it; otherwise it keeps the name it arrived with.

Response: `result`, `key`, `bytes`, `filename`, `contentType`, `source` (`upload` or `received`); for a body upload also `bodyFormat` (`binary` or `base64`) and `sha256`.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Saved-attachment key you choose: 1-128 characters, letters, digits and . _ - : @ + =, starting with a letter, digit or +. Doubles as the default filename when sent, so prefer a real filename such as invoice_template.pdf.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: Promote this received attachment (ref from mail/pop) instead of uploading a body. 404 if it has expired.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: The file's name, WITH its extension (e.g. INV-261010-2AW8T.pdf). It sets the content type the file is served with (a .pdf opens as a PDF), the name a browser saves it under, and the default attachment name in mail/send. Characters other than letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-' become '_'. Without it the file is named after its key and served as application/octet-stream.

get.summary: Fetch a saved or received attachment
get.description: Pass exactly one of `key` (saved store) or `ref` (received store). Returns base64 in `data`. Over 4096 KB the response carries a presigned `url` (valid `expiresInSeconds`) instead, because a Lambda proxy response caps at 6 MB; `url=true` forces that at any size. `source` is `saved` or `received`. With `download=true` or `view=true` the response is instead a 302 redirect to a short-lived (15-minute) link to the file itself - saved under its filename, or shown in the browser - so a single URL works in a browser address bar. With `password` (or `password64`) a protected PDF is served unlocked: the API decrypts it into an unprotected copy (kept for a day) and returns that copy in every form - `data`, `url`, `download` and `view` - so `view=true&password=...` opens straight in the browser. The response adds `unlocked`, `encrypted` and `originalBytes`. A wrong password is 422 (`passwordIncorrect`); PDFs up to 10240 KB can be unlocked.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Saved-attachment key.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: Opaque 10-character ref of a RECEIVED attachment, from the attachments list of mail/pop. Received attachments expire 7 days after the email arrived.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Return a presigned download URL instead of inline base64.

parameters.name: download
parameters.description: true = answer 302 straight to the file, which the browser saves under its filename. One URL to paste into a browser.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: true = answer 302 straight to the file, shown in the browser (a PDF opens in a tab). Not with download.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Password of a protected PDF (open or owner password). The file is served UNLOCKED: an unprotected copy, so a browser shows it without asking for the password (and data/url return the unlocked copy). Ignored for a PDF that is not encrypted; 400 for a non-PDF.

parameters.name: password64
parameters.description: Base64 of the UTF-8 password.

302.description: download=true or view=true: redirect (Location header) to the file.

Location.description: A presigned URL for the file, valid for a few minutes, with Content-Disposition set from filename (attachment for download=true, inline for view=true).

get.summary: Search inside an attachment without downloading it
get.description:
Extracts text from the attachment and searches it, so a test can assert on document content without pulling the bytes into the harness. Handles PDF, docx/xlsx/pptx, and plain text / CSV / JSON / HTML; anything else falls back to printable-string extraction. Identify the file with `key` (saved) or `ref` (received).

PDF text is laid out as it appears on the page: one line per visual line, a tab between columns (label and value cells), a single space between words. Call `mail/attachments/text` to see exactly what is searched.

Exactly one search mode: literal (`text` / `text64`), regular expression (`regex` / `regex64`, Python syntax), or LoadRunner-style boundary capture (`left` + optional `right`, or `left64` / `right64`).

Whitespace is flexible by default: a space in `text`, `left` or `right` matches any run of spaces, tabs or line breaks, so `Invoice number INV-261002-1TFJP` matches across the column gap and `Total including GST` matches whether or not the label wraps. In boundary mode leading whitespace after `left` is skipped, captures are trimmed, and with no `right` the capture stops at the end of the cell (tab or line end). Empty captures are not counted (`emptyMatches`). `exact=true` restores character-for-character matching.

Password-protected PDFs: pass `password` (or `password64`). Either the user (open) or owner password works; PDFs with only an owner password (restrictions) open without one. RC4 40/128, AES-128 and AES-256 are supported. A missing or wrong password is 422 with `passwordRequired` or `passwordIncorrect`.

`in=metadata` searches the PDF document properties (Title, Author, Keywords and custom keys such as InvoiceNumber), one `Name<TAB>value` line each; `in=all` searches both. Every result has `page` (1-based; null for metadata or non-PDF files). Regex and boundary modes add `values`: the flat list of captures. A `count` of 0 adds `caseInsensitiveCount` and a `hint`. `document.characters` near zero means the document has no text layer (a scan, no OCR), not that the term is absent. Extraction (10 s) and matching (3 s) run under wall-clock guards and return 400 rather than a gateway timeout. Files over 20480 KB are refused (400).

get.summary: Is this the same document? Compare two attachments
get.description:
Compares two files from the attachment stores - typically the PDF that arrived by email (`ref`) and the copy downloaded from the application and saved with mail/attachments/save (`otherkey`). Name the first with `key` or `ref` and the second with `otherkey` or `otherref`; any combination works.

Reports three things: `sameBytes` (byte-for-byte identical, plus each file's `sha256`), `sameText` (the extracted text is the same line for line - runs of whitespace and blank lines are ignored, so a different column gap is not a difference) and `sameProperties` (the PDF document properties). **`same` is `sameText`**: a PDF generated a second time usually differs in its creation date and internal IDs, so its bytes change while its content does not. `verdict` says which case applies in words. When the text differs, `differences` lists the changed lines with their page numbers (up to 50; `differenceCount` is the total). `propertyDifferences` lists document properties that differ, without affecting `same`.

Protected PDFs: `password` / `password64` opens the first file, and the second too unless `otherpassword` / `otherpassword64` is given. A missing or wrong password is a 422 as for mail/attachments/text.

get.summary: Generate a PDF: pages, exact size, text placed by page, password
get.description:
Generates a real PDF (Helvetica text, one compressed content stream per page, prose-like filler) and stores it like any other attachment: under `key` in the SAVED store, or as a temporary attachment with a `ref` (7 days). Either way mail/send, mail/attachments/get, find, text and compare take it.

Size it by `pages` (what parsers, OCR and processing time feel) and/or `kb` (what upload limits and mail size caps feel; exact to the byte). Place known text with `prepend64` (top of page 1), `overwrite64` (middle page) and `append64` (bottom of the last page) - by page, not by byte offset, because splicing bytes into a PDF corrupts it. `placement` in the response says where each value went, so a test can assert both that the text is there and on which page.

`password` protects it with AES-256; mail/attachments/find without it is then a 422 passwordRequired. `title`, `author`, `subject` and `meta64` set document properties. The same parameters with the same `seed` give the same bytes; no creation date is written.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Save the PDF in the SAVED store under this key (kept until deleted). Without key it is a temporary attachment with a ref (kept 7 days), usable wherever ref= is.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Filename ('.pdf' appended if missing). Default document-<hash>.pdf.

parameters.name: pages
parameters.description: Number of pages, 1-500 (clamped). Without pages or kb: 1 page; with only kb: as many pages of text as fit, then padding.

parameters.name: kb
parameters.description: Exact file size in KB (1-6000; 1-2048 with a password). Filler text compresses about 3:1, so the size is reached with an incompressible private-data stream that viewers ignore. A size too small for the pages asked for is a 400 with minKb.

parameters.name: prepend64
parameters.description: Base64 of UTF-8 text for the first lines of page 1 (the first thing a reader extracts). Each value starts on its own line and wraps only at spaces; newlines start new lines. WinAnsi (Western European) characters only - anything else is a 400 listing the code points. Up to 4000 characters.

parameters.name: overwrite64
parameters.description: Base64 of UTF-8 text placed in place of filler lines, centred on the middle page (page (pages+1)/2, rounded down). Each value starts on its own line and wraps only at spaces; newlines start new lines. WinAnsi (Western European) characters only - anything else is a 400 listing the code points. Up to 4000 characters.

parameters.name: append64

get.summary: Browser page for uploading saved attachments
get.description: A drag-and-drop HTML page for humans (not scripts). Files go straight to S3 via mail/attachments/upload/url, so files up to 102400 KB work. Returns text/html.

get.summary: Presigned S3 POST for uploading a large saved attachment
get.description: Returns `{url, fields}` for a presigned S3 POST. Submit them as multipart/form-data with every field first and the raw file LAST (form field name `file`); the bytes go straight to S3, so neither the API Gateway 10 MB nor the 6 MB Lambda payload limit applies and there is no base64 inflation. The 102400 KB cap rides in the policy as content-length-range and is enforced by S3, whatever `size` claims. Valid for `expiresInSeconds` (900). S3 answers 201 on success. That is the STORE limit - what mail/send can carry is 28000 KB, and much less if it has to reach a real mailbox. Pass `filename` to name the file; the name and content type are then part of the returned `fields`.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Saved-attachment key you choose: 1-128 characters, letters, digits and . _ - : @ + =, starting with a letter, digit or +. Doubles as the default filename when sent, so prefer a real filename such as invoice_template.pdf.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: The file's name, with its extension. Stored with the file (and its content type set from the extension), exactly as filename on mail/attachments/save.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Declared size in bytes; checked against the cap up front so an oversized file fails before upload.
